ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an annular conducting coil a is laid flat on a horizontal tabletop, and a vertical solenoid b is fixed directly above a; their axes coincide. The solenoid is connected with a power supply and a sliding rheostat to form the circuit shown in the figure. If the slider P of the sliding rheostat is slid downward, how will the pressure FN of coil a on the horizontal tabletop change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The pressure FN of coil a on the horizontal table will increase
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, coil a is drawn on a horizontal tabletop (or horizontal plate surface), in an annular shape; directly above it is a vertically placed solenoid b, and the two are approximately coaxial. On the right side of the solenoid there is a power supply and a sliding rheostat connected, and beside the sliding rheostat the slider P is marked. According to the meaning of the problem, when the slider P is slid downward, the resistance connected into the circuit between the slider and the lower end decreases. Then reason: if the connected resistance decreases, then the total resistance of the circuit decreases, the current in solenoid b increases, the magnetic field produced by the solenoid strengthens, and the magnetic flux through the lower annular coil a increases accordingly. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current in coil a must hinder the increase of the original magnetic flux, so coil a and the upper solenoid b behave as mutually repelling each other. Solenoid b is above a, so the direction of this repulsive force on coil a is downward; the downward magnetic force on coil a increases, causing its pressure FN on the horizontal tabletop to increase.
